title: Frontend: File Explorer
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind File Explorer. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({nodes=[{id:root,title:Root,children:[{id:a,title:A}]}]}). Render a nested disclosure list. Node li[data-node=ID] contains button[data-open=ID] for folders (children array) or [data-select=ID] for files. Folders start collapsed; clicks select and toggle them. [data-testid=selected] displays selected ID or None. Use stable IDs and aria-expanded on folder buttons. New file input and Add file[data-action=add] append to first root folder with sequential IDs new1,new2. Trim names, reject blanks with Name required and duplicate sibling titles with Name exists. Delete[data-delete=ID] removes a subtree and clears selection.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use stable node IDs, parent relationships, and a separate ordered-child representation or an immutable nested reducer.
alternativeApproaches: Add optimistic server operations with version conflicts and reversible mutations.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Duplicate sibling name; rename; delete selected node.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
